messages:
Priya Kapoor: Heads up — ACME (acct_8971) flagged a month-end mismatch. Dashboard shows 12,432 tokens for March, invoice shows 14,017. They noticed a plan-tier bump at 2026-03-31 23:58 UTC but totals still off by +1,585 tokens on the invoice.
BillingBot: metering job completed: window_end=2026-03-31T23:59:00Z, processed=2026-03-31T23:59:30Z, rows=4,512, backfill=false
Carlos Mendez: do we have any late postbacks from on-prem connectors for that acct? last week had a flurry.
Ethan Li: running a quick query on raw_metering table now — suspicious pattern: a batch of postbacks with event_ts between 23:59:10 and 00:02:20 with identical client_request_id prefixes. Could be retry duplication.
Maya Patel: if retries didn't dedupe before aggregation, invoice job might count them but dashboard rollups (cached per-route) may dedupe earlier. Different code paths.
Priya Kapoor: ACME says they saw a spike from their private deployment around cutoff. They uploaded logs showing retries after 23:59 due to transient network error.
Jules Tran: repro steps I ran locally: 1) insert two identical meter rows with same client_request_id and different received_ts; 2) run aggregation pipeline; 3) invoice-side job picks both if dedupe index not enforced.
Jules Tran: SQL snippet I used:

```
INSERT INTO raw_metering (account_id,client_request_id,tokens,event_ts,received_ts)
VALUES ('acct_8971','req-abc-123', 1024, '2026-03-31T23:59:05Z','2026-03-31T23:59:12Z'),
       ('acct_8971','req-abc-123', 1024, '2026-03-31T23:59:05Z','2026-04-01T00:00:45Z');
```

Then run: `SELECT SUM(tokens) FROM invoice_agg WHERE account_id='acct_8971' AND period='2026-03';`

Result included 2,048 tokens for the duped id.
BillingBot: dedupe_window_ms is set to 300000 (5m) for the dashboard rollup worker, invoice aggregator uses ingestion_id dedupe which relies on a unique constraint that was briefly disabled during the midnight deploy rollback (2026-03-31T23:57-23:59 UTC).
Carlos Mendez: ah — we had a deploy rollback in that window. Dedupe constraint toggled in migrations. That could explain double-counts on invoice side.
Ethan Li: timeline matches ACME's postbacks. Invoice job ran after the rollback and saw both rows. Dashboard rollup worker had already processed first row and deduped in cache TTL, so it shows the lower number.
Maya Patel: impact scope — likely small subset: accounts with on-prem postbacks + retries within 5m of cutoff and handled during the rollback window. Need to identify affected invoices.
Priya Kapoor: action items: (1) Identify affected accounts and amounts, (2) issue temporary credits where necessary, (3) re-run invoice aggregation with dedupe constraint re-enabled and produce corrected invoice if delta> $50.
Jules Tran: query to locate suspects:

```
SELECT account_id, client_request_id, COUNT(*) as cnt, SUM(tokens) as tokens
FROM raw_metering
WHERE event_ts BETWEEN '2026-03-31T23:55:00Z' AND '2026-04-01T00:05:00Z'
GROUP BY account_id, client_request_id
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;
```

Use that to generate candidate list.
BillingBot: queued a backfill job: job_id=bkfill-177654-03, priority=high, will run in ~12m. It will re-run invoice aggregation with dedupe constraint enforced and emit a delta report.
Carlos Mendez: I'll run reconciliation and prepare spreadsheet of (acct, dashboard_tokens, invoice_tokens, delta, suggested credit). Priya, can you escalate billing credits for any deltas > $20?
Priya Kapoor: yes, I can approve up to $200 per account in emergency credits. Escalate anything above to finance.
Ethan Li: note for engineering — add a post-deploy checklist to ensure dedupe constraints never disable across midnight rollouts. Also add a short TTL buffer on invoice aggregator matching dashboard dedupe logic.
Maya Patel: I'll draft a customer message template for ACME and similar accounts: explain postback retries + deploy timing, describe remediation and whether they'll see a corrected invoice or a credit.
Priya Kapoor: thanks team. Will update ACME once the backfill job finishes and we have the delta csv. :thumbsup:
